newsitem.title: CHINA: China arrests more than 10 linked to bus bombs.
newsitem.headline: China arrests more than 10 linked to bus bombs.

text.p: Chinese authorities have arrested more than 10 people for allegedly organising a string of bus bomb attacks in a mainly Moslem, northwestern city in February that left nine dead, police said on Monday.

More than 10 suspects had been rounded up for alleged involvement in the bomb attacks in Xinjiang's regional capital, Urumqi, a police officer said by telephone. He declined to provide further details.
A Chinese source quoted police in Urumqi as saying the suspects were members of a previously unheard of pro-independence group, the National Liberation Front.

Bombs planted on three buses blew up within minutes of each other in Urumqi on February 25 in an apparently coordinated attack that coincided with funeral rites in Beijing for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
The bombings killed nine and wounded 74.
All of the suspects in police custody were of the Moslem Uighur ethnic minority, the source, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Prosecutors were expected to indict the suspects, the source said without specifying the charges.
Police had launched a hunt for five suspects who were still on the run, the source said.

Exiled ethnic Uighurs, who want to set up an independent "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, have claimed responsibility for the bombings and vowed to stage more attacks until they gain freedom for their Moslem homeland.
The People's Daily, mouthpiece of the Communist Party, on Monday quoted Qiao Shi, head of China's parliament, as saying China should take a firm stand against separatists in Xinjiang.

"We must firmly oppose national separatism and religious extremist forces and safeguard the dignity of laws and the fundamental interests of the people of various ethnic groups," said Qiao, who sits on the Communist Party's omnipotent seven-member Politburo standing committee.
The fight against separatism would continue to top the government's agenda, he said.

"We must always guard against and strike hard at activities to split the unification of the motherland and undermine unity among people of various ethnic groups," said Qiao during a stopover in Xinjiang on Sunday following a visit to Europe.
"It will be our top priority work at present and a task for a long time to come," he said.
"We must always bear in mind the idea that Han people cannot live without the ethnic minorities and the ethnic minorities cannot live without the Han people," he said.
Hans account for about 90 percent of China's population of 1.2 billion but are the minority in Xinjiang.
Last month, six Uighurs were charged with hooliganism and endangering social order in connection with rioting in Yining in Xijiang on February 5-6.
The riot began as a demonstration for Xinjiang independence and turned violent, leaving nine people dead and 198 injured.

Xinjiang, bordering Afghanistan, Pakistan and three mostly Moslem Central Asian states, was shaken last year by bombings and assassination attempts on officials and Moslem leaders regarded as favouring Beijing.
Authorities intensified a crackdown on separatists and underground religious activity.
